'''Hkuqo''', officially the '''Federal Republic of Hkuqo''', is a country in [[Central Ayuma]]. Located on the western edge tip of the [[Moksha Mountains]], it shares land borders with [[Ukhdari]] to the north, [[Jau]] to the east and [[Jshain]] to the south, and [[Taval]] to the east across the sea. The [[Diairesi Sea]] lie to the southwest of the mainland, and the [[Tasa Bay]] to the west. Hkuqo has the longest coastline on the [[Middle Acrola]], spanning over 50 islands and four traditional geographic regions. It has a population of over 22 million. [[Tanshiva]] is the nation's capital and largest city, followed by [[Dhamasol]] and [[Vindasira]].

Hkuqo is considered the cradle of Alqiran civilisation and the birthplace of [[Wikipedia:Aristocracy|aristocracy]], Central philosophy, [[Wikipedia:Literature|Central literature,]] historiography, [[Wikipedia:Political science|political science]], major scientific and mathematical principles, and theatre. The Ancient Hkuqoan were organised into independent city-states that spanned the coastline. The [[First City-state period]] began in the fourth century BFA. The subsequent period saw the height of Hkuqoan culture and influence in antiquity. Hkuqo was annexed by [[Ealdorii]] in the second century BFA and became an integral part of the [[Ealdorii Empire]] until the end of the first century. The [[Second City-state period]] lasted from the third till the eighth century, where the [[Alqir Empire]] controlled Hkuqo. 

After the [[Kaastini Invasion]] of [[Alzuria (region)|Alzuria]], Hkuqo and the rest of the [[Alqir empire]] were fragmented, starting the [[Third City-state period]]. The northern half of Hkuqo during this time was controlled the the Alzurians. Following a protracted war of independence in the 1480s, Hkuqo emerged as an independent Kingdom 1487. The [[Kingdom of Hkuqo]] was restored after the [[Treaty of Brimsha|Treaty of Brimsha,]] after the Defeat of Golden. It joined the side of the ___ during the [[Great Imperial War]], A short-lived republic was established in 1783 but faced [[civil strife]] and the challenge of resettling internal refugees and, culminating in a [[royalist dictatorship]]. Hkuqo endured [[military occupation]] during the Red War, resulting in prolonged political instability, leading to [[Gireru Irade]] leading a [[coup in 1707]]. The country began transitioning to democracy in 1729 after the death of [[Gireru Irade]] a year prior, leading to the current Second Republic.

Owing to record dictatorship from 1700 to 1725, Hkuqo is a [[Wikipedia:Developing country|developing country]] with a [[Wikipedia:Developing country|low-income economy]]; its low standard of living has been damaged by a two-decade-long debt crisis that emerged in the wake of the [[Great Crash]]. Shipping and [[Wikipedia:Tourism|tourism]] are major economic sectors. Hkuqo is part of multiple international organisations and forums. The country's rich historical legacy is reflected partly by its 20 [[Global World Heritage Sites]].
